newsitem.title: FINLAND: U.S. data helps Helsinki end weak session higher.
newsitem.headline: U.S. data helps Helsinki end weak session higher.

text.p: Shares ended a weak session higher on Thursday, given a late fillip by Nokia which rose after U.S. jobless data boosted treasuries and some stocks.

The HEX index picked up 0.47 percent to 2,201.9 after spending most of the session down, with volume fair at 324 million markka, only 24 percent of it in Nokia, which closed off its 210 markka session high but up 1.80 at 209.40.

But brokers said the market remained edgy and -- in the absence of domestic factors -- was unnerved by the risk of a key U.S. rate hike after the elections, with a potential short-term pointer due in more U.S. economic data on Friday.
U.S. October unemployment would be the main focus and the bourse was expected to stay thin and cautious, they said.
"It is very much up to what happens in the U.S. overnight and tomorrow ... the data is very important," one broker said.
End-month window-dressing by proprietary traders bolstered some shares, particularly Merita which ended flat, said one broker noting the stock's sudden sharp gains during the month.
"Nokia looks technically weak since it did not manage to stay above 210 markka, which is a quite a critical level," another said, adding the stock could fall to 190.
Forest industry shares continued weak due to increasing expectations the sector will not see an upturn soon: "Hopes for an upturn in forest industry are definitely fading," said one.
Kemira at one stage touched its 49.50 markka issue price but closed at 49.60, down 0.30 markka.
